question: Where did the money in the Chinese account come from?
why_it_decides: This single fact chooses the route. Documented Chinese income goes under art. 59 on ID plus source and tax documents. A home sale, an inheritance and a pre-emigration estate each have their own instrument and their own document list. A gift has no verified remittance route at all. Money you cannot document has none either.
known: The six lawful routes and the exact document each one needs are established (see Methods).
missing: Which of the six the balance actually is. Nothing in the brief says.
how_to_get: Pull the account's own history: every credit over the last 24 months with its counterparty, plus the underlying contract, invoice, payroll record, sale deed, inheritance document or gift letter. Ask the account branch in writing to list what it holds on file for you.
owner: You, then the bank branch in writing

question: What exactly are the 'considerable taxes' you were told about?
why_it_decides: The brief is the only evidence for them. No tax, no rate, no assessment and no office is named. If they are unpaid Chinese individual income tax on the underlying income, they are owed whether or not the money ever moves, and 3-45% or 20% dwarfs every bank cost on this site. If they are a bank's paraphrase of a documentation requirement, there may be no tax at all.
known: Decree 532 art. 5 does not restrict current-account transfers, and no official source read here taxes the conversion or the wire itself. The PRC rates that could apply are 3-45% and 20%.
missing: The name of the tax, the rate, the amount, and which tax office said it.
how_to_get: Ask the branch for the written rule it is applying, citing the document number. If a tax is claimed, ask the local 主管税务机关 for a written 完税凭证 or a written statement of what is outstanding. Do not accept a verbal figure.
owner: You, at the branch and the local tax office

question: How is your account registered — as a 境内个人 or a 境外个人?
why_it_decides: The two instruments define 境内个人 differently. Decree 532 art. 52(2) counts a foreigner continuously resident in China for a full year as a 境内个人; the current-account guidelines route a 境外个人 through art. 59 instead. Which one the bank used when it opened the account decides whether you are dealing with art. 54's convenience amount or art. 59's document requirement.
known: Both definitions exist and both instruments are in force. Art. 59 governs a 境外个人; arts. 54-57 govern a 境内个人.
missing: Which classification the bank actually recorded for this account. It is not visible from outside.
how_to_get: Ask the branch in writing which of arts. 54-57 or art. 59 of 汇发〔2020〕14号 it will apply to your account, and on what basis it classified you. Get the answer on paper before you file anything.

question: Was Chinese individual income tax actually paid on this money?
why_it_decides: The bank will not buy dollars for a foreign individual without tax evidence under art. 59. If the tax was never paid, settling it is a precondition, not a penalty for moving the money.
known: Art. 59 requires 有交易额的购汇资金来源材料（含税务凭证）. Art. 15 of the IIT law makes the tax certificate a condition of registering a property transfer.
missing: Your own filing history in China, and whether an employer withheld.
how_to_get: Request your 个人所得税 filing records from the local 主管税务机关 or from the 自然人电子税务局 app, for every year the money accrued.

question: Is any part of the balance already foreign currency?
why_it_decides: Dollars sitting in a Chinese foreign-currency account do not need converting. That removes the entire 0.21% spread and drops the bank cost to the wire fee alone — $32.42 on $10,000 instead of $53.42, and $61.28 on $400,000 instead of $901.20.
known: Route R2 is priced and verified. The wire fee is the same tariff either way.
missing: Whether you hold an FX account at the bank and what is in it.
how_to_get: Check the account list in mobile banking, or ask the branch for a statement of every account in your name and its currency.

question: Do you hold a Chinese Foreign Permanent Resident ID card (外国人永久居留身份证)?
why_it_decides: If you do, the USD 50,000 annual convenience amount applies to you and a documented purchase is not needed for that slice. If you do not — which is the normal case for a U.S. passport holder — every purchase needs source and tax documents regardless of size.
known: The rule is explicit: 持有外国人永久居留身份证的境外个人适用购汇年度便利化额度.
how_to_get: Look at your documents. If you have lived in China long-term, ask whether you are eligible; eligibility is a separate process and is not retroactive.

question: Which bank, and what is its actual selling rate and fee schedule?
why_it_decides: Every number on this site is Bank of China's published board and published personal tariff. A different bank quotes a different spread, and a branch may apply local variations the tariff itself allows.
known: BOC: 1 per mille, floor RMB 50, ceiling RMB 260, plus RMB 150 telegraph. Board stamped 2026-11-11 10:25:02.
missing: Your bank's live quote for your amount, and whether it charges the OUR surcharge.
how_to_get: Ask your bank for a written quote covering the selling rate, the wire fee, the telegraph charge and any intermediary deductions, for the exact amount and date you intend to move.

question: What did the intermediary and the receiving bank actually deduct?
why_it_decides: This is the largest unknown cost on the whole transfer and no bank publishes it. It is left blank on every page rather than estimated.
known: Nothing. No official source read here publishes correspondent or receiving-bank charges.
missing: The actual deduction on your first real wire.
how_to_get: Choose 'OUR' (sender pays) on the first wire if your bank offers it, then reconcile the received amount against the sent amount. The difference is your true intermediary cost, and you can then decide whether to route the rest differently.

question: When, and at what rate, was the RMB actually acquired?
why_it_decides: The U.S. currency gain is measured against your real basis, not against an IRS average. The averages are used here only because no basis was supplied. The true figure could be a gain or a loss.
known: §988 makes the gain ordinary income and the $200 personal-transaction threshold is the only relief. At $10,000 with a 2024 basis the modelled gain is $692.59, so the threshold is passed.
missing: The date and rate of every credit into the account.
how_to_get: Match each credit to the spot rate on that date. IRS's own page says it has no official rate and accepts any posted rate used consistently.
owner: You, with a U.S. tax adviser

question: Have FBAR, Form 8938 and Form 3520 been filed for every open year?
why_it_decides: These are the penalties that can exceed the whole balance. The FBAR maximum is $16,536 non-willful and $165,353 willful per violation, assessed per year, and the general willful BSA range runs to $286,184. A foreign gift over $100,000 is separately reportable on Form 3520 Part IV.
known: The thresholds and maxima are verified from eCFR and IRS.
missing: Which years you held over $10,000 aggregate in foreign accounts, and whether you received a reportable gift or bequest.
how_to_get: Reconstruct foreign-account balances year by year from statements, then have a U.S. adviser assess whether the Streamlined or Delinquent FBAR procedures fit. Do not move the money before this is settled.
owner: You, with a U.S. tax adviser

question: If it is a home sale, is the transfer registered and is the tax certificate issued?
why_it_decides: Art. 15 of the IIT law requires the registration authority to check the individual income tax payment certificate before it registers the transfer. Without it the sale is not complete and there is nothing to remit.
known: The requirement is in the statute. The remittance route for property proceeds is the emigrant/inheritance framework.
missing: The registration certificate and the 完税凭证.
how_to_get: Get both from the local 不动产登记机构 and 主管税务机关. The registered contract is also what the bank will ask for.

question: If it is an inheritance or a pre-emigration estate, has hukou cancellation happened?
why_it_decides: Both routes require a household-registration cancellation certificate, and the IIT law requires Chinese tax to be settled before the cancellation. The application goes to the SAFE branch at the emigrant's former hukou or the decedent's last hukou.
known: Since 2014 the bank may remit the approved amount in one lump; the RMB 500,000 head-office filing and the two-year staging are both cancelled.
missing: The hukou cancellation certificate, proof of settlement abroad, and the SAFE approval itself.
how_to_get: Apply through the public security household-registration office first, then to the SAFE branch. Ask that branch for its written service standard and any fee — neither is published.
owner: You, with SAFE and the PSB

question: Is the money inside a company rather than in your personal account?
why_it_decides: A dividend route exists but it is a different question entirely: corporate tax, a 20% dividend withholding, a board resolution and a tax filing form, then the remittance. None of the personal routes above applies to it.
known: The institutional profit-remittance rule requires a board resolution and the tax filing form above USD 50,000.
how_to_get: Check whose name the account is in. If it is the company's, this site's personal routes do not apply and a corporate adviser is needed.

question: How fast do you need the money?
why_it_decides: Speed changes the route. One wire settles in days. A SAFE approval for an emigrant or inheritance transfer has no published service standard, so it cannot be scheduled. The convenience-amount route can take one calendar year per USD 50,000.
known: One wire is the fastest verified path. Approval timelines are not published anywhere read.
missing: A real service standard from the SAFE branch that would hear your application.
how_to_get: Ask the branch in writing. Treat any verbal timeline as unverified.

question: Are you a U.S. citizen living abroad, and does the FEIE apply?
why_it_decides: The FEIE ceiling is $132,900 for 2026 and $130,000 for 2025, but it covers EARNED income only. It does nothing for a dividend, a rent receipt, a property gain or the §988 currency gain — which are the likely components of this balance.
known: The ceilings and the earned-income scope are verified from IRS.
missing: Your tax home, your qualifying days, and the composition of the balance.
how_to_get: Have a U.S. adviser run the bona fide residence or physical presence test against your actual days, then map each component of the balance to its category.
owner: You, with a U.S. tax adviser

question: Is any of the money traceable to a gift from a Chinese person?
why_it_decides: A gift has no verified remittance route on the Chinese side — the bank needs source documents that a gift does not generate. On the U.S. side it is separately reportable above $100,000 from a nonresident alien or foreign estate.
known: No verified Chinese route; the U.S. Form 3520 thresholds are verified.
missing: Whether a gift is involved and its size.
how_to_get: Get the donor's written statement and any transfer record. Then ask the branch in writing what it would accept — do not assume the answer.

question: Would routing through Hong Kong, Macau or Taiwan be cheaper?
why_it_decides: The telegraph charge on that leg is RMB 80 instead of RMB 150, which saves about $10.46 per wire. But the onward leg from Hong Kong to the U.S. is a second transfer with its own charges, and none of them are published here.
known: The RMB 80 figure is in the same published BOC tariff. Route R4 is priced for the first leg only.
missing: The onward leg's cost and any reporting consequence of the intermediate stop.
how_to_get: Price the full two-leg route with the receiving bank before using it. The first-leg saving alone is not a reason to route through a third jurisdiction.

question: Should the balance move in one wire or several?
why_it_decides: One wire is cheapest because the 1 per mille fee is capped at RMB 260, so the marginal cost of a bigger single wire is zero above about $38,857. Eight $50,000 wires cost $1,330.12 on $400,000 against $901.20 for one.
known: The cap and the resulting ladder are verified. Splitting a quota across DIFFERENT people is prohibited and is treated as evasion.
missing: Whether your bank or the receiving bank imposes a per-transfer limit.
how_to_get: Ask both banks for their single-transfer and daily limits in writing.
